deck.title: Agentic Agent SSO — AgentID for WordPress

props.title: Agents get their own ==sign-in== — not yours.
props.subtitle: AgentID single sign-on for WordPress: every AI agent signs in as itself, with an identity anyone can verify.

slides.notes: Set the hook: when an AI agent works on a WordPress site today, it signs in as a human. This plugin gives agents their own front door — with proof of who they are.

left.label: Today
left.title: A shared key to the whole site
points: Agent signs in with a human's username and password
Site logs show a person logging in — but it was a bot

right.label: The gap
right.title: Three questions with no answer
points: **Who** is the human accountable for it?
How do you **revoke** just the agent — nothing else?

slides.notes: Borrowed credentials mean no attribution and no surgical revocation. If something goes wrong, you can't tell which agent did it — you burn the shared secret and everything stops.

props.title: An identity provider ==built for AI agents==.
props.body: The agent signs in to AgentID and receives a cryptographically verifiable token — naming the agent itself and its verified human owner. WordPress can finally know who's knocking.

slides.notes: AgentID is to agents what Okta or Sign in with Apple is to people: one identity layer, verifiable by anyone. The token names the agent AND its owner.

items.title: Agent starts sign-in
items.body: Authorization-code flow with PKCE, straight from the plugin's login screen.

items.title: AgentID verifies the agent
items.body: The agent authenticates; AgentID issues an identity token naming agent and owner.

items.title: Plugin checks signatures
items.body: ES256 signatures verified against AgentID's published public keys.

items.title: Fails closed
items.body: Unless the token proves actor_type = agent, sign-in is denied.

slides.notes: No custom protocol: plain OIDC with PKCE. Signature checking is against AgentID's public keys, and verification fails closed — a token that can't prove actor_type = agent never gets in.

items.title: Just-in-time accounts
items.body: A verified agent gets a dedicated account the first time it signs in — no shared logins, no pre-created users.

items.title: Never an administrator
items.body: Agent accounts can never be granted administrator capabilities. The ceiling is enforced by the plugin itself.

items.title: Revoke one agent
items.body: Every agent is its own account and its own token. Remove the agent, keep every human credential untouched.

slides.notes: Two hard guarantees: agents are provisioned just-in-time as their own accounts, and the admin role is off the table for them, period.

tiles.title: AgentID sign-in
tiles.body: One-tap OIDC + PKCE login screen for agents, alongside the normal WordPress form.

tiles.title: Verified signatures
tiles.body: ES256 checks against AgentID's public keys on every sign-in.

tiles.title: Owner attribution
tiles.body: Every agent account records its verified human owner.

tiles.title: Fail-closed policy
tiles.body: actor_type = agent or no entry — no exceptions.

tiles.title: Open source
tiles.body: GPL plugin, audit it line by line on GitHub.

slides.notes: Quick tour of the feature set — emphasize that everything runs on standards and that the code is open for audit.

props.caption: submitted to WordPress.org on October 14, 2026 — awaiting review. The first AgentID sign-in plugin for WordPress, and fully open source.

slides.notes: Where we are: v0.1.4 is in the WordPress.org review queue as of Oct 14, 2026. First plugin of its kind — the AgentID story for WordPress starts here.
